title: Future time
subtitle: Present continuous, will, be going to, and present simple

blocks.text: For the form of the present continuous, see Unit 1.
Things we want to do in the future but have not arranged are called **intentions**. We do not use the present continuous for intentions. We use **be going to** instead.

blocks.correct: I'm **going to become** an explorer when I grow up.
blocks.incorrect: I'm **becoming** an explorer when I grow up.

blocks.text: We do not use the present continuous for predictions. We use **will** or **be going to** instead.
blocks.note: Do you think you'll **enjoy** your trip to Berlin next week? (not you're enjoying)

rows.person: I / you / he / she / it / we / they
rows.question: **Will** I/you/he/she/it/we/they **go** …?

rows.example: The new airport **will be** the biggest in Europe.
You'll **have** a great time in the Bahamas.
We'll **help** you get ready for your holiday.
I know! I'll **go** to China this summer.

blocks.text: With offers which are questions, we use **Shall** with **I** and **we**.
blocks.note: Shall I drive you to the airport?

blocks.incorrect: We'll **visit** my grandma this weekend. (not for a fixed arrangement)

rows.negative: He/she/it **is not (isn't / 's not) going to travel** …
rows.question: **Is** he/she/it **going to travel** …?

rows.negative: You/we/they **are not (aren't / 're not) going to travel** …
rows.question: **Are** you/we/they **going to travel** …?

rows.example: I'm **going to become** an explorer when I grow up.

rows.use: Predictions (often with evidence we can see)
rows.example: It's **going to rain**, so take an umbrella.
The new airport **is going to be** the biggest in Europe.
